newsitem.title: USA: Repap debt recoups Friday's sharp losses.
newsitem.headline: Repap debt recoups Friday's sharp losses.

text.p: The assurance of financial liquidity for Repap Enterprises Inc quelled bankruptcy talk on Monday and rescued the company's debt from losses as deep as eight points on Friday, traders said.

Unit Repap Wisconsin Inc's 9-7/8 percent debt was offered at 92 bid-94 offer at midday on Monday compared with levels as low as 85 on Friday. The 9-1/4 percent debt was seen offered at 95 with no bid.
The debt had traded above par before shareholders of Avenor Inc blocked a proposed acquisition.

Stephen Larson, Repap's president and chief operating officer, told Reuters on Monday that a C$20 million increase in bank credit from Toronto-Dominion bank would be enough to meet bond and interest payments into the third quarter.
Larson also denied rumors that the company may seek bankruptcy protection following the failed Avenor bid. Repap is now preparing to sell operating units of the company on an individual basis.
The underlying value of Repap's units' comforted bondholders, traders said.
"It appears that New Brunswick and Wisconsin (units) will be sold and there should be more than enough money from the sale for repayment of the debt," one international high-yield debt trader said.
Shares of Repap gained 0.13 into mid-afternoon on Monday after losing 0.54 to close at 0.55 on Friday.
